rationale: This is a mechanical cross of two archive signals — the industry-neutral 3-year accrual leg from IndustryNeutralChronicAccrualDecay with the gross-margin-trend conditioner from AccrualBuildupDecayingProfit — so it is a robustness permutation rather than a new mechanism, and given how correlated declining gross profitability and declining asset turnover are, it is unlikely to deliver information beyond the existing best signal.

The expression is internally consistent (NEG(invch) correctly signs inventory buildup, NEG(GROWTH(cogs)) correctly signs contracting production) and the motivation — that the wrong-signed FMB slope on the raw version may come from pooling structurally different inventory intensities — is a genuine diagnosis rather than a cosmetic tweak, though it remains a single-operator variant whose upside is bounded by whether industry neutralization happens to fix a sign contradiction that could equally be a small-cap or scaling artifact.

The stated economics do not survive scrutiny — the change makes the *most bullish* observations firms that are liquidating working capital while asset turnover decays, i.e. shrinking, likely-distressed firms, which is a hypothesis the proposal asserts rather than argues — and rank-to-zscore is otherwise a scaling variant that reintroduces outlier sensitivity to the very leg the archive winsorized.

The second difference of operating-capital intensity is a genuinely distinct temporal construct from the levels, first differences, and three-year sums already in the archive, the signs are internally coherent, and the only real risk is that acceleration is mechanically mean-reverting and noisy — which is itself an informative test outcome.

Loss frequency over five years is a coarse but economically independent quality conditioner unlike every continuous trend/volatility measure already tried, and the signs are correct (NEG of profitable-year frequency ranks loss-prone firms high, multiplying the accrual leg toward the short side); the main caveats are the heavy ties from a six-valued conditioner and the inconsistent use of IND_RANK on one leg but plain RANK on the other.

The stock-versus-flow comparison on a held-fixed conditioner is a legitimate design question and the expression matches the hypothesis, but the level of non-cash working capital scaled by sales is close to the well-documented net-operating-assets/operating-asset-bloat anomaly, so any result must be shown to survive controls for that known effect rather than rediscover it.
